You **should not** use your friend’s secret key for testing (or any other) payments in your own app.  

### Why that’s a bad idea

| Reason | Consequence |
|--------|-------------|
| **Security** | The secret key has full control over your friend’s Stripe account (charges, refunds, data access, etc.). If it ends up in the wrong hands, someone could lock your friend out or steal money. |
| **Account boundaries** | Stripe keys are tied to a specific Stripe account. You can only initialize the SDK, create customers, charge, etc., for that account. If you try to create charges for your own business or use endpoints that belong to your own account, Stripe will reject the request. |
| **Compliance & Trust** | Using someone else’s key violates Stripe’s terms of service and can lead to account suspension or legal problems. It also breaks the “trust boundary” between you and your friend. |
| **Data leakage** | Any logs or metadata you capture (IP addresses, order ids, etc.) will be associated with their account, not yours. |
| **Audit & bookkeeping** | Your friend’s account will show all activity, making reconciliation impossible and confusing future reporting. |

### What to do instead

1. **Create your own Stripe account or use a sandbox/test account.**  
   *You can set up a free Stripe account for the app you’re developing. Stripe always gives you a *test mode* environment where you can use test keys and test card numbers.*

2. **Enable test mode**  
   * In the Stripe dashboard, make sure you’re in Test mode. Use the Test Publishable and Secret keys that Stripe generates for you.  
   * Your app can detect the environment (e.g., using a `STRIPE_MODE=test` flag) and switch keys accordingly.

3. **Use test card numbers**  
   * Stripe supplies a list of safe test card numbers (https://stripe.com/docs/testing).  No real money ever moves.  

4. **Consider a separate account for production**  
   * When you ship your app, you’ll want a production Stripe account. You can copy the integration logic, just swap the keys in your environment variables or secrets management tool.

5. **If you need shared access while still keeping things clean**  
   * You can add yourself as a user with limited privileges on your friend’s account, or use “Connected Accounts” (if you’re building a platform). In either case, you still use the keys that belong to the relevant account.

### Bottom line

Always use your own keys (or keys that explicitly belong to an account you control) for any Stripe integration. That keeps your security, compliance, and data integrity intact. Happy building!
